name: "Sandman" Kevin Sleeper
caption: Defended the promotion's own Apex Championship in its own naming-document broadcast before dropping it off-panel some time before the promotion's next served card.

name: "Prime Suspect" Jimmy King
caption: Challenged twice for gold in the promotion's earliest served broadcasts, falling short of both the Apex and Television Championships.

name: Jack Payne
caption: Won his debut match by submission, then upset the promotion's own United States Champion by count-out with an assist from a rival's handler.

name: "The Cowboy" Zach James
caption: A journeyman who dropped his first two served matches, to Jack Payne and later to Luc Stevens.

name: Dirty Bird
caption: Debuted opposite Dark Hawk on the promotion's own first served pay-per-view and later fell to Tony Lattanzio on a weekly card.

name: Dark Hawk
caption: Won his debut match on the promotion's own first pay-per-view, then won the Television Championship a month later.

name: Cypris
caption: A self-described former EAW Hardcore Champion who held and lost the promotion's own Apex Championship within its earliest served weeks.

identity.note: A same-named RSPWF Top 200 stub (1999, #110) carries only the tag BSW, not this promotion's own acronym; nothing ties the two records together.

name: Snakeye
caption: Held the promotion's own Hard Knocks Championship (formerly the Iron Man Championship) by the time of its second served weekly card, though the belt was not defended there.

name: "The Real X-Man" Phoenix X
caption: A self-described former FRW and EAW wrestler who won both the Television and Apex Championships within the promotion's own earliest served weeks, aided each time by a rival's interference.

identity.note: Billed under the fuller ring name "Phoenix X"; a large cluster of unrelated "Phoenix" records elsewhere on the registry share only the bare first half of that name.

name: JR Kidd
caption: Challenged for the Television Championship on the promotion's own first served pay-per-view and came up short.

name: "The Pitbull" Tanke Brute
caption: Won the promotion's own vacant United States Championship in a bout his own opponent all but conceded.

name: Tiny Tayshaun Walker
caption: Lost the promotion's own World Heavyweight Championship in his own farewell match, then left the promotion outright.

name: "Talon" James Trent
caption: Won the promotion's own World Heavyweight Championship by interference on its first served pay-per-view and carried it into the promotion's following served cards.

name: Alexander King
caption: Retained the promotion's own Iron Man Championship inside a Hell in a Cell on the promotion's first served pay-per-view, hours before the title was renamed the Hard Knocks Championship.

name: Shane Diamond
caption: Challenged for the promotion's own Iron Man Championship inside a Hell in a Cell on its first served pay-per-view and lost.

identity.note: Two unrelated same-named records already exist (a tenured 1998 AICW wrestler and a 1998 RSPWF Top 200 stub tagged ICW); neither shares this promotion's own acronym or dates.

name: Luc Stevens
caption: The promotion's outgoing commissioner, fired and re-signed as a wrestler by its incoming owner, who went on to hold the United States Championship.

identity.note: A same-named RSPWF Top 200 stub (climbing from #153 in 1998 to #25 in 1999) carries only the tags FWF, BSW and PWP, not this promotion's own acronym.

name: Asylum
caption: A self-described former TEWA World Heavyweight Champion who won the promotion's own Television Championship before losing it a month later.

identity.note: An unrelated same-named record (a 2000 SWA/Seltor wrestler) shares no axis with this promotion.

name: X
caption: A newcomer who issued a wordless challenge to the promotion's own roster before losing his only served match to Big Bully Brandon.

name: Dan Rose
caption: The promotion's founding president, who sold the company and departed on its first served pay-per-view.

name: Rich Armani
caption: Bought the promotion on its first served pay-per-view and renamed one of its titles within minutes of taking over.

name: Trent Richardson
caption: Named the promotion's commissioner by its new owner on the following night's broadcast.

name: Jeremy
caption: One of the promotion's own broadcast commentators across its earliest served cards.

name: Jack Law
caption: One of the promotion's own broadcast commentators, introduced by name on its first served pay-per-view.

name: Benz

name: Teddy Rimino
caption: The promotion's own ring announcer from its second served card onward.

name: Tre Banks
caption: Wagered his own career on a match with Jimmy King on the promotion's first served pay-per-view, lost, and left the promotion.

name: Big Bully Brandon
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 1999: #61, tagged BSW, AWA, WAV. Carries no tenure entry: none of the tagged federations is a held promotion, and the poll records where a wrestler was tagged, never a run this record could date.
caption: Won a federation's own vacant United States Championship by knocking his own opponent out with a bag of pennies before the bell, then lying down to be pinned rather than cover him himself.

tenures.source: Named as "3B" Big Bully Brandon, leader of a stable called the Badasses, across the promotion's own first three served broadcasts; won the promotion's own vacant United States Championship on 17 January 1999 and won a tag match on 10 February 1999.
